nodes.content: Enable safe sim-to-real transfer for robotic peg insertion when friction and clearance changes are indistinguishable before contact.
requirements: Achieve ≥90% insertion success across held-out friction–clearance combinations using at most 20 real adaptation trials.
Keep peak contact force below 20 N during adaptation and deployment without privileged state observations.

nodes.content: Use low-force probes for 20-trial Bayesian friction–clearance inference from wrist wrench and proprioception, then 18 N upper-confidence-limited impedance insertion.
Can low-force contact probes distinguish friction from clearance using wrist wrench and proprioception within 20 adaptation trials?
Twelve ≤10 N lateral dithers yield ≤15% median relative error for friction and clearance inferred from wrench–displacement traces.
On calibrated held-out pairs, run 12 ≤10 N dithers, fit wrench–displacement posteriors, and compare parameter errors with 15%.
Run 12 ≤10 N lateral dithers per calibrated held-out friction–clearance pair; fit wrench–displacement posteriors and compute median relative errors.
Across 24 held-out pairs, 12 dithers yielded 11% friction and 13% clearance median relative errors; peak force was 9.7 N.
After e1 met 15% errors, probe six near-degenerate held-out pairs with 12 ≤10 N dithers; recalculate parameter errors.
On six near-degenerate pairs, 12 dithers produced 24% friction and 31% clearance median relative errors despite 9.8 N peak force.
Retain the validated 12-dither baseline and add ≤10 N axial micro-pushes for near-degenerate pairs with 31% clearance error.
Replace fixed 12-dither protocol with 12 dithers plus up to eight ≤10 N axial micro-pushes for posterior-ambiguous pairs; reassess errors.
Across 30 held-out pairs, run 12 dithers and ≤8 ambiguity-triggered micro-pushes; measure 18 N-capped insertion success and peak force.
Peg30 evaluation log records probe traces, adaptation counts, insertion outcomes, and peak forces for 30 held-out friction–clearance pairs.
How should posterior uncertainty set insertion speed and impedance when clearance estimates remain ambiguous after safe probing?
Randomize posterior-conditioned speed–impedance schedules on Peg30 pairs; measure insertion success and peak force under an 18 N wrench limit.
Peg30: posterior-conditioned schedules achieved 28/30 insertions versus 24/30 fixed, with 19.1 N peak force and ≤20 adaptation trials.
Stress-test e3’s selected speed–impedance schedule on 30 fresh ambiguous pairs with 10-ms wrench delay; log insertion success and peak force.
With 10-ms wrench delay on 30 fresh ambiguous pairs, insertion success fell to 25/30 and peak force reached 22.4 N.
Retain posterior-conditioned scheduling’s 28/30 baseline, but add delay-aware braking and a predictive 15 N cutoff after the 22.4 N overshoot.
Use delay-aware force prediction from wrench and proprioception to brake or retract before forecast peak contact force exceeds 15 N.
Can a 15 N predictive cutoff prevent >20 N impacts under 10-ms wrench delay without reducing ambiguous-pair success below 90%?
With 10-ms wrench delay, 15 N predictive braking keeps peak force below 20 N and achieves ≥27/30 ambiguous-pair insertions.
Test d2’s 15 N predictive brake on 30 ambiguous pairs under 10-ms delay; record success, peak force, adaptation trials.
Implement 15 N predictive braking on 30 ambiguous pairs with 10-ms delay; log insertion success, peak force, and adaptation counts.
Under 10-ms delay, 15 N predictive braking inserted 28/30 ambiguous pairs; peak force was 18.6 N, with ≤20 adaptation trials.
Test e5’s brake on 40 fresh held-out pairs at 10-ms delay; measure insertion success, peak force, and adaptation trials.
Brake40 evaluation log contains insertion outcomes, peak-force traces, and adaptation counts for 40 fresh held-out pairs under 10-ms delay.
Use a passive remote-center-compliance wrist and 18 N slip clutch with wrench-guided spiral search, avoiding friction–clearance identification.
Can passive compliance and an 18 N slip clutch prevent transient >20 N impacts during spiral search on tight-clearance pairs?
Audit Brake40’s peak-force traces for missed 1-kHz transients, then test 18 N-clutch spiral search on matched tight-clearance pairs.
Brake40 audit found two >20 N transients; clutch-assisted search inserted 37/40 matched tight-clearance pairs, peaking at 19.3 N.
Prioritize clutch-assisted search for tight-clearance pairs: 37/40 inserted at 19.3 N peak; Brake40 showed two >20 N transients.
Fuse wrist-wrench and contact acoustics to detect stick–slip, then trigger jam-release micro-rotations behind an 18 N clutch.
Building on d3’s clutch, calibrate wrench–acoustic stick–slip detection and micro-rotations; test insertion success and peak force on 40 held-out pairs.
Derive jam-onset thresholds from Brake40’s force traces, then collect synchronized wrench–acoustic trials to tune clutch-protected micro-rotations.
Brake40-v2 augments original force traces with jam-onset labels and linked new synchronized wrench–acoustic trials plus clutch micro-rotation settings.
Does contact-acoustic stick–slip detection improve jam recovery over wrench-only triggering on held-out friction–clearance pairs?
Compare Brake40 wrench-only thresholds against Brake40-v2 wrench–acoustic triggering on held-out pairs; measure jam recovery, insertion success, peak force.
On 40 held-out pairs, wrench–acoustic triggering recovered 17/20 jams versus 12/20 wrench-only; insertion success reached 37/40, peaking at 19.4 N.
After e7, stress-test Brake40-v2 acoustic triggers versus wrench-only on 40 motor-noisy held-out pairs; log jam recovery and peak force.
On 40 motor-noisy pairs, acoustic triggering recovered 9/20 jams versus 12/20 wrench-only; false triggers reached 14/40.
Retain acoustic triggers in quiet runs (17/20 versus 12/20 jam recoveries); use wrench-only in noisy runs (12/20 versus 9/20).
Calibrate a motor-noise gate, then compare gated acoustic/wrench-only jam recovery against both fixed triggers across 40 mixed-noise pairs.
Calibrate Brake40-v2’s motor-noise gate against quiet/noisy baselines; compare gated versus fixed triggers on 40 mixed-noise pairs for jam recovery.
Brake40-v3 updates Brake40-v2 with calibrated noise-gated trigger routing and 40-pair mixed-noise jam-recovery comparisons.
Can clutch-protected micro-rotations release deep stick–slip jams on high-friction pairs without exceeding 20 N?
On deeply jammed high-friction pairs, ≤3 clutch-protected ±2° rotations release ≥80% of jams while peak force stays below 20 N.
Induce 30 deep high-friction jams, apply ≤3 clutch-protected ±2° rotations, and measure release fraction and peak force.
Induce 30 mixed-noise high-friction deep jams; test Brake40-v3’s gated triggering and ≤3 clutch-protected ±2° rotations; log release and peak force.
Brake40-v3 released 25/30 deep high-friction jams within three clutch-protected ±2° rotations; maximum 1-kHz force was 19.6 N.
Test Brake40-v3’s three ±2° rotations on 30 fresh deep high-friction jams across noise levels; log release and 1-kHz peak force.
On 30 fresh deep jams, three ±2° rotations released only 21/30; one transient reached 20.7 N at 1 kHz.
Despite 25/30 initial releases, suspend ±2° rotations after 21/30 replication and a 20.7 N transient; test 15 N-clutched retraction.
Revise n5’s trigger comparison to evaluate 15 N-clutched retraction against recorded ±2° outcomes, retaining quiet-acoustic/noisy-wrench routing and logging force.
Using Brake40-v3 routing and e9/e10 baselines, test 15 N-clutched retraction on 30 fresh deep jams; measure release and 1-kHz force.
Brake40-v4 replaces ±2° jam recovery with 15 N-clutched retraction and adds 30-jam release and 1-kHz force logs.
Can wrench–acoustic sensing flag incipient jams at least 20 ms before clutch slip across mixed motor noise?
Annotate clutch-slip onset in Brake40-v3/v4 force logs; replay mixed-noise triggers, measuring ≥20-ms warning fraction and false alarms.
Gated alerts preceded clutch slip by ≥20 ms in 24/30 mixed-noise jams; three false alarms occurred across 40 insertions.
Prospectively test Brake40-v4’s gated alerts and retraction on 40 mixed-noise insertions; log ≥20-ms pre-slip warnings, false alarms, and 1-kHz forces.
Brake40-v4 flagged 17/20 jams ≥20 ms before slip across 40 mixed-noise insertions; two false alarms, 19.2 N peak, 37/40 succeeded.
Adopt gated pre-slip retraction, not suspended rotations: early warnings replicated (24/30, 17/20), with 37/40 insertions and 19.2 N peak.
